name: NAMI (National Alliance on Mental Illness) Family-to-Family
description: Free 8-week education program for family members and caregivers of people with mental health conditions.

sections.title: About Family-to-Family
sections.text: NAMI Family-to-Family is a free, 8-session educational program for family members, significant others, and friends of people living with mental health conditions. The program is taught by trained family members who have firsthand experience supporting loved ones with mental illness. It provides education about mental health conditions, treatment approaches, and evidence-based communication strategies.

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.text: The Family-to-Family curriculum covers understanding major mental health conditions including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, anxiety disorders, and others. Participants learn about treatment options including medications and therapy, how to handle crises, effective communication and problem-solving skills, advocacy strategies, and self-care for caregivers.

sections.title: How the Program Works
sections.text: Family-to-Family classes meet weekly for 8 sessions, each lasting about 2-2.5 hours. Classes are offered in-person and online through local NAMI affiliates across the United States. The small group format allows participants to share experiences and support each other while learning from trained peer instructors who understand the caregiving journey.

sections.title: How to Enroll
sections.text: Family-to-Family is completely free. To find a class near you, visit nami.org or contact your local NAMI affiliate. Classes fill up quickly, so early registration is recommended. Participants should be family members or friends of someone with a mental health condition. The program has helped hundreds of thousands of families since its creation.
